title: Android Studio and Gradle
description: Build and test Android projects with Gradle, using Android Studio's Java and the Android SDK.
notes: Covers ./gradlew builds and unit tests of an Android project. The Mac has no Java of its own, so the command must say where Android Studio's is: JAVA_HOME="/Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home". The SDK is found through the project's local.properties or ANDROID_HOME.
Gradle's working folders in ~/.gradle can be changed, and the SDK only read: a build cannot install SDK packages or accept licenses. Do that in Android Studio first.

Not covered: ~/.gradle/gradle.properties and ~/.gradle/init.d, which can hold signing passwords, repository keys and scripts that every build runs. A project that needs a value from there fails; pass it on the command line or record a pack on top of this one.
~/.android can be changed, because every build writes there. It also holds the debug signing key and the key that lets this Mac talk to your devices.
A Gradle daemon that was started outside the conversation is not confined by the sandbox. Use --no-daemon in a conversation.
Downloading dependencies needs the network to be allowed in Agentic Session Tools. The emulator and installing on a device were not tried.

recorded.by: sandbox-discover, with Android Studio's Java 21 and Gradle 9.5, then the same under the pack's folders alone
